AGENDA
REGULAR MEETING OF THE TRAFFIC SAFETY COMMITTEE
OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
THIS AGENDA HAS BEEN AMENDED TO INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING NOTICE:
This Traffic Safety Committee meeting of March 3, 2021 is being held pursuant to Executive Order N-25-20 issued by California Governor Gavin Newsom on March 12, 2020 to further the State's efforts to control the spread of COVID-19 Coronavirus. Any and all Traffic Safety Committee Members may attend and participate by teleconference/virtual meeting. Members of the public may also attend by teleconference in order to observe and provide public comment during the meeting. The meeting will not be livestreamed. If you wish to participate, the following process must be followed.
The meeting will begin promptly at 6:30 p.m. so please prepare and join the meeting in advance of 6:30 p.m. The Zoom Meeting ID is 898 5536 9975 (direct link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89855369975). You will be muted upon entry. The host will unmute you when it is your turn to speak. If you wish to speak during the meeting, email cityclerks@pvestates.org with (1) your name, (2) the project address on which you'd like to speak, and (3) the phone number and/or Zoom name from which you will be calling in to the meeting no later than 5:00 PM on March 3, 2021.
If you wish to show any visual aids while you speak during the meeting, you may submit a PDF version (maximum 20 slides) no later than 12PM on March 3, 2021 to rolson.hrgreen@pvestates.org Each member of the public is allotted 3 minutes maximum to present.
CALL TO ORDER
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ROLL CALL (6:30 PM)
APPROVAL OF AGENDA
COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC
Members of the audience are invited to address the Committee at this time on items that are not otherwise on the agenda. Per the California Government Code Section 54954.2, the Traffic Safety Committee is prohibited from discussing or taking immediate action on any item not on the agenda unless it can be demonstrated that the item is of an emergency nature, or the need to take action arose subsequent to the posting of the agenda.
APPROVAL OF ACTION MINUTES
a)
Traffic Safety Committee Action Minutes of December 2, 2020.
Recommendation: Review and Approve.
Action Minutes
OLD BUSINESS
1.
Proposed Restriping of Palos Verdes Drive North at Paseo Del Campo/Via Alameda and Additional Information Regarding the Effect of Lane Width on Speed
Recommendation: Recommend to the City Council to approve restriping southbound Palos Verdes Drive North at the intersection of Paseo Del Campo/Via Alameda to align the single through lane north of the intersection with the inner through lane on the south side of the intersection and remove the existing lane offset at the intersection.
Staff Report
NEW BUSINESS
2.
Overview of Current Coastal Zone Parking Restrictions on Paseo Del Mar and Palos Verdes Drive West and Recommended Improvements to Signage and Curb Painting
Recommendation: Streets and Parks staff refresh the existing red curb areas and paint curbing in front of all fire hydrants and bus stops along Paseo Del Mar and Palos Verdes Drive West, and review all parking signage in this area to ensure that the signs are accurately demarcating the beginning and ending of any restricted parking areas, and provide additional signage in locations where restrictions are in place, but are not marked due to missing or poorly located signage.
Staff Report
Correspondence
3.
Discussion of Coastal Area On-Street Parking Concerns and Protection of General Public Access
Recommendation: 1) Obtain public input relative to the impact of on-street parking along the Coastal Zone; 2) Identify additional information, considerations or analysis required prior to making recommendations to the City Council regarding modifications to the existing on-street parking regulations in the Coastal Zone; and 3) Request that staff prepare a study with recommended actions that balance the need to maintain public access with the public safety concerns of residents.
Staff Report
4.
Consideration of Interim Improvements to Relieve Traffic Congestion Along the Palos Verdes Drive West (PVDW) Corridor and Next Steps of The PVDW Corridor Feasibility Study Process Next Steps for the Palos Verdes Drive West Corridor Feasibility Study Process
Recommendation: Review and Discuss the information and options provided and, if no further information is required of staff, recommend to the City Council which, if any interim improvements to the Palos Verdes Drive West (PVDW) corridor should be considered to address traffic congestion.
Staff Report
5.
Review of the City’s Traffic Calming Application Process and Consideration of Any Desired Changes
Recommendation: Review the current traffic calming application process and provide direction to staff regarding any elements they would like to see reviewed or updated; content added, removed, or modified; as well as any procedural changes they would like considered or implemented.
Staff Report
6.
Creation of a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Section on the City's Website to Address Some Common Traffic Questions
Recommendation: Consider suggested Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) related to traffic and parking rules and regulations to be included on the City's website and provide any additional suggestions.
Staff Report
OTHER ITEMS
ADJOURNMENT TO WEDNESDAY, JUNE 2, 2021, 6:30 P.M.
Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (310) 378-0383, at least 72 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
